answer: Price admission on a surge curve. Each new account locks a refundable deposit, and that deposit doubles for every other account admitted in the same epoch through the same inviter or funding source, then decays back to base. An honest newcomer arriving alone pays the base, one pearl on a string. A farmer pushing N fakes through one gate pays about 2^N, so the summit of the curve comes fast, and spacing them out across epochs slows the farm to a juniper's pace. Deposits return after a year of passing work.
